subject: ela
name: English Language Arts
course: Thematic Critique, Rhetorical Analysis & Expository Composition
title: Grade 8 English Language Arts: Thematic Critique, Rhetorical Analysis & Expository Composition
overview: Grade 8 English Language Arts cultivates analytical reading of complex literature, rhetorical dissection of informational texts, evidence-based argument composition, and public academic discourse.
competencies: Cite comprehensive textual evidence to analyze central ideas, themes, and author viewpoints.
Evaluate the credibility, reasoning, and rhetorical strategies of diverse informational texts.
Craft well-organized, defensible argument and informative essays with precise citations.
Communicate effectively in collaborative academic presentations and structured seminars.

modules.title: Literary Critique, Rhetorical Irony & Thematic Synthesis
modules.description: Analyzing how dialogue propels action, analyzing points of view, and critiquing how modern texts draw upon traditional myths.

topics.title: Propelling Action Through Dialogue and Incidents
topics.description: Analyzing how lines of dialogue or specific incidents in a story provoke a decision or reveal character traits.

topics.title: Dramatic and Situational Irony
topics.description: Analyzing the effects of differences in character and reader perspective creating suspense and irony.

topics.title: Allusions and Mythological Archetypes in Modern Literature
topics.description: Analyzing how contemporary authors transform material from mythology and classical literature.

modules.title: Rhetorical Analysis of Speeches & Conflicting Arguments
modules.description: Evaluating conflicting arguments on public policy topics, detecting rhetorical fallacies and emotional manipulation.

topics.title: Delineating and Evaluating Argumentative Claims
topics.description: Assessing whether an author's reasoning is sound and evaluating the relevance of supporting evidence.

topics.title: Analyzing Two or More Texts with Conflicting Points of View
topics.description: Analyzing how two authors writing on the same topic present conflicting interpretations of key facts.

modules.title: Formal Academic Arguments & Multi-Source Research
modules.description: Drafting sophisticated argumentative essays with precise claims, counterclaims, warrants, and MLA citations.

topics.title: Argumentative Essays with Comprehensive Counterclaims
topics.description: Writing well-reasoned essays acknowledging opposing viewpoints and defending claims with authoritative evidence.

topics.title: Independent Research Synthesis and Presentation
topics.description: Conducting self-directed research projects, compiling formal annotated bibliographies, and delivering digital presentations.
